handbookNote: Louisiana Revised Statutes Title 35 (Notaries Public and Commissioners), including the Remote Online Notarization Act (R.S. 35:621-630), together with the Louisiana Civil Code articles on authentic acts (Civil Code arts. 1831-1853), donations and testaments (arts. 1541-1580.1, as simplified by 2025 Act No. 30), sale and mortgage (arts. 2439-2442, 3287-3289), matrimonial agreements (art. 2331), and successions/forced heirship (arts. 871-876, 1493-1495), plus the Code of Civil Procedure's succession-inventory and small-succession articles (arts. 3131-3432) -- price matches this project's established $9.99 Notary tier, but Louisiana is a fundamentally different, much richer case than every other state's notary track: Louisiana is a civil-law jurisdiction whose notaries hold quasi-attorney authority to draft authentic acts (acts of sale, mortgages, successions, donations, and other legal instruments) that no other US state's notaries may perform, hold their commission for life rather than a fixed renewable term, and sit a state-administered exam offered at least twice yearly (with licensed attorneys exempt from the online pre-assessment) -- hence the substantially larger, 9-topic question bank here versus a typical single-state notary track
